tasks.acceptance: model.Workflow and model.WorkflowOverride carry AuditConvergeOn; engine/projectconfig.go parses workflow.audit_converge_on with the same string-type warning as its twin; ResolveWorkflowLayers merges task override over project config over the built-in `all`; tp config --resolved reports it with its source on a repo with no configuration. Section 7 row 1 passes.
tasks.closed_reason:
audit_converge_on now exists on the workflow types and resolves to the built-in all, the deliberate asymmetry with review_converge_on's blocking that section 2.1 measures.
- model.Workflow gains AuditConvergeOn string and model.WorkflowOverride the *string twin, counted by IsEmpty so a config setting only this field is not read as empty; verified by the package building and by TestResolveWorkflowLayers_AuditConvergeOn constructing both.
- engine/projectconfig.go admits audit_converge_on to knownWorkflowKeys and parses it with review_converge_on's exact string-type warning; verified by an assertion over parseWorkflowOverride({"audit_converge_on":7}) requiring the field nil and the warning 'workflow.audit_converge_on: expected a string, ignored'.
- ResolveWorkflowLayers merges task override over project config over the built-in via pickString; verified in TestResolveWorkflowLayers_AuditConvergeOn that the task override wins over project, that project applies with no override, and that an invalid stored value resolves raw rather than clamped.
- tp config --resolved reports the field with its source; verified by two CLI tests run through the freshly built binary: TestAuditConvergeOnDefaultAll gets value all / source default on a repo with no configuration, and TestAuditConvergeOnResolvedNamesItsSource gets project then override as the layers are added.
- Section 7 row 1 passes, and its mutant was constructed rather than reasoned about: the built-in was first shipped as AuditConvergeOnBlocking and both default assertions were observed failing with 'expected all, actual blocking' (engine configresolve_test.go:100, cli auditconvergeon_test.go:37) while every other assertion in the same tests stayed green, which is what isolates the default from the precedence; switching the built-in to AuditConvergeOnAll turned both green. Dogfooded on tp's own repo: config --resolved reports audit_converge_on all/default beside review_converge_on blocking/default. Gate green end to end, exit 0.
Out of scope, each owned by a later task in this cycle: the write sinks (set --workflow still rejects audit_converge_on as an unknown workflow field, which is what keeps TestAuditGate_NoEscapeHatchFromTheGate green until reverse-gate-guard reverses it), the consuming-sink validation, ValidAuditConvergeOn and its hint, config --extract hoisting and validate --project, the unattended fence, the severity predicate, by_severity, and the documentation.

tasks.title: Assert the resolver consults exactly two layers
tasks.acceptance: A test asserts task override beats project config beats built-in, and that neither a TP_AUDIT_CONVERGE_ON environment variable nor an --audit-converge-on flag changes what resolves — the mutant is adding either layer to engine.ResolveWorkflowLayers. Section 7 row 2 passes.
tasks.closed_reason:
v0.37.0 §7 row 2: three tests assert audit_converge_on resolves through exactly two layers, and each was proved discriminating by running its named mutant.
- Precedence: TestResolveWorkflowLayers_AuditConvergeOnConsultsExactlyTwoLayers/'the two layers rank' asserts task override beats project config beats built-in (all/blocking/all) in internal/engine/configresolve_test.go.
- No environment layer: the sibling subtest sets TP_AUDIT_CONVERGE_ON=blocking — the value neither real layer names — and asserts all resolves in all three configurations, so the assertion is not the tautology an unset variable would give; TestAuditConvergeOnHasNoEnvironmentLayer repeats it end to end through a tp config --resolved child, asserting value=all and source=default.
- No flag layer: TestAuditConvergeOnHasNoCommandFlag asserts tp audit/config/set/run/review each refuse --audit-converge-on with exit 2 and 'unknown flag: --audit-converge-on', so silent acceptance is what fails.
- Mutant A (env layer at the TOP rank of engine.ResolveWorkflowLayers): all three environment assertions red (got blocking, wanted all), 'the two layers rank' green, TestAuditConvergeOnHasNoEnvironmentLayer red, the flag subtests and the shipped row-1 tests green.
- Mutant A2 (same layer at the LOWEST rank, below project config): only the built-in case red, the two rank-pinning cases and 'the two layers rank' green — so the row is caught at any rank, not just the top.
- Mutant B (a real --audit-converge-on flag registered on tp audit): only the audit subtest red, config/set/run/review green, both environment tests green — per-command discrimination.
- Reverted both mutants (git diff on internal/engine/configresolve.go and internal/cli/audit.go empty) and the quality gate passed on the final tree: suite-state wrapper ok, golangci-lint 0 issues, deadcode and complexity clean, exit 0.

tasks.title: Reject an illegal stored value at the audit sinks with ExitValidation
tasks.acceptance: An illegal value stored in .tp/config.json or in a task file makes tp audit --record and tp audit --status exit ExitValidation, a code distinct from the write sinks'. Section 7 row 3's consume half passes.
tasks.closed_reason:
Both audit consuming sinks now refuse an illegal stored audit_converge_on with ExitValidation, and the refusal precedes every write.

- An illegal value stored in .tp/config.json makes both `tp audit <spec> --record` and `tp audit <spec> --status` exit 1 (ExitValidation): TestAuditConvergeOn_InvalidStoredInProjectConfigExitsValidation asserts the exit code, the quoted value and the hint through the parsed error envelope.
- An illegal value stored in a task file's workflow block does the same on both sinks: TestAuditConvergeOn_InvalidStoredInTaskFileExitsValidation. The two layers are separate tests, not subtests of one fixture, because they are reached differently — dropping the project layer from resolution leaves the task-file test green and reddens the project-config one (mutant M5, run).
- The code is ExitValidation (1) and is distinct from the write sinks' ExitUsage (2): the guard is `engine.ValidAuditConvergeOn` with `engine.AuditConvergeOnHint`, byte-identical to ReviewConvergeOnHint as section 2 requires ("the same hint as review_converge_on"). Mutant M1, mapping both consume sinks to ExitUsage, reddens four assertions across the two tests.
- Section 7 row 3's consume half passes; the write half stays with converge-write-sinks. Row 3's named mutant ("map both to one code") is M1 above. Two further half-graded mutants were built and run: deleting only the --status guard (M3) and deleting only the --record guard (M4) each redden their own half and leave the other green.
- The ordering hazard did NOT require reordering, and the reason was measured rather than assumed. runAuditRecord already resolves the workflow once into wfPre at the top, before EnsureReviewState and recordAuditRoundEntry, so the guard was placed there; nothing above that line writes. Mutant M2 — the same guard moved onto the later `wf` resolve, after the round is stored — was built and run: every exit-code assertion stayed GREEN while only "a refused --record wrote no audit-round-1.ndjson" and "... no state.json" reddened, which is the defect an exit-code-only check cannot see.
- Verified by running, not by reading: on the shipped binary before the change, `tp audit spec.md --record` over a tree storing "bogus" exited 0 and wrote .tp-review/spec/audit-round-1.ndjson plus state.json; the new tests were watched failing on exactly those five assertions before the guards were added. After the change the same tree exits 1 and creates no .tp-review directory at all, while a legal `blocking` still records round 1 — dogfooded with a freshly built /tmp/tp-dev/tp.
- Quality gate green: `./scripts/check-suite-state.sh && golangci-lint run && ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh && ./scripts/check-complexity.sh` exited 0 (cli 47.7s, engine 30.4s, all packages ok; golangci-lint "0 issues."; deadcode and complexity silent-clean).

tasks.title: The severity predicate that grades a round under the resolved policy
tasks.acceptance: One engine predicate over (rows, policy): under `all` clean iff no non-PASS row; under `blocking` clean iff no non-PASS row carries a blocking severity, where `error` blocks and a severity outside the enum, JSON null, an absent key or a non-string value all block. Four fixtures, one per unrecognised shape; the mutant that must fail is grading a row with no usable severity as advisory. Section 7 rows 5, 6, 7 and 8 pass.
tasks.closed_reason:
- One engine predicate over (rows, policy): engine.AuditRowsClean(rows []map[string]any, convergeOn string) bool in internal/engine/auditclean.go, a pure function of its two arguments because section 2 stamps clean at record time rather than recomputing it live.
- Under all, clean iff the round holds no non-PASS row: the loop returns false on the first row AuditRowIsPass rejects, and any policy literal other than the exact string blocking takes that arm, so an unrefused value grades under the stricter default.
- Under blocking, clean iff no non-PASS row carries a blocking severity: auditSeverityBlocking names the advisory half of the vocabulary (warning, info) and blocks by exclusion, so error blocks and a string outside the enum, JSON null, an absent key and a non-string value all block. The comparison is byte-for-byte like AuditRowIsPass, so WARNING is outside the enum and blocks, which keeps section 4 identity error plus unrecognised equals the blocking rows true. It never consults engine.SeverityRank, which is built for the review words and ranks every audit severity unknown.
- Four fixtures, one per unrecognised shape: TestAuditRowsClean_UnusableSeverityBlocks subtests a string outside the enum, JSON null, an absent key, and a value that is not a string, each unclean under blocking and under all.
- The mutant that must fail is grading a row with no usable severity as advisory: built as blocking iff the severity type assertion equals error, and run. It reddened exactly the four row-8 subtests at auditclean_test.go:77, the blocking assertion, while rows 5, 6 and 7 stayed green. Three further named mutants were run for discrimination: grade on status alone reddened rows 5 and 6 only; return clean whenever the policy is blocking reddened rows 7 and 8 only; special-case info only reddened row 6 alone, which is why section 7 asserts it apart from row 5. The real implementation then turned all six functions and four subtests green.
- Section 7 rows 5, 6, 7 and 8 pass: TestAuditRowsClean_InfoIsAdvisory, _WarningIsAdvisory, _ErrorBlocksUnderBoth and _UnusableSeverityBlocks all PASS, plus _PassRowsAreNotGraded (PASS rows carry severity null, so a predicate over rows of any severity would report every all-PASS round unclean) and _UnknownPolicyGradesAsAll.
- Quality gate green: check-suite-state.sh, golangci-lint run with 0 issues, check-deadcode.sh and check-complexity.sh all passed, exit 0.

tasks.title: Stamp clean at record time, both directions, and never re-grade on read
tasks.acceptance: tp audit --record stamps the round's clean from the predicate under the policy resolved at record time; recording under all then setting blocking without re-recording leaves every round's clean unchanged in state.json AND as tp audit --status reports it; a round recorded under blocking keeps clean:true after the knob returns to all. The mutant is re-grading each stored round from its rows in the reporting path. Section 7 rows 9 and 9b pass.
tasks.closed_reason:
tp audit --record now stamps clean from engine.AuditRowsClean under the resolved audit_converge_on; the predicate had no production caller before this.

- clean is stamped once at record time from the predicate under the resolved policy: internal/cli/audit_record.go replaces `clean := findings == 0` (the `all` policy written as an equality) with engine.AuditRowsClean(rows, wfPre.AuditConvergeOn); countAuditFindings becomes parseAuditRows and returns the rows, because the blocking predicate grades each non-PASS row's severity and a tally has discarded it
- the policy is taken from wfPre, the resolve that precedes every state write, not from the wf resolved after recordAuditRoundEntry: the round is stored before that second resolution, so a stamp from it would grade a round already in a store section 2 declares immutable
- recording under all then setting blocking without re-recording leaves every round's clean unchanged in state.json AND as tp audit --status reports it: TestAuditRecord_StampSurvivesTighteningTheKnob asserts the reported audit_rounds[].clean, consecutive_clean, converged and the verbatim state.json bytes over two rounds; row 9's named mutant (re-grade each stored round from its rows in the reporting path) reddens the first three and leaves the bytes green, exactly as the spec predicts
- a round recorded under blocking keeps clean:true after the knob returns to all: TestAuditRecord_StampSurvivesRelaxingTheKnob was red before the fix for the expected reason, and asserts findings:1 beside clean:true so the verdict is visibly not the count; run at both stored layers because a stamp reading only one of them is green on the other
- five mutants built and run in an rsync copy, red/green matrix recorded: row 9's named mutant, row 9b's read-side floor (leaves row 9 wholly green), re-grade only the derived signals (leaves audit_rounds[].clean honest), store the old equality while reporting the new stamp (leaves the --record payload honest), and drop the project layer (reddens only the project subtest)
- gate green: ./scripts/check-suite-state.sh && golangci-lint run && ./scripts/check-deadcode.sh && ./scripts/check-complexity.sh, exit 0; dogfooded on the freshly built /tmp/tp-dev/tp — recorded under blocking gives findings 1 / clean true, and clean survives the knob returning to all in both state.json and --status
